data.name: Haaji
data.gender_notes: Haaji is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A person who has performed the Hajj pilgrimage to Mecca. In Islamic tradition, the Hajj is considered one of the Five Pillars of Islam and is a mandatory religious duty for able Muslims at least once in their lifetime. The name Haaji carries the meaning “Pilgrim” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Haaji usually hope their child will grow to embody pilgrim and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embarks on a spiritual journey to seek closeness to Allah (swt)
data.etymology: Haaji belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Pilgrim.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Haaji total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_arabic.name: حاجي
in_arabic.meaning: المزارعون، الذين يستجلبون الماشية إلى المكان المقدس للحج.
in_arabic.long_meaning: الحاجي هو لقب يُطلق على الأشخاص الذين يعملون في المزارع أو الزراعة، ويستجلبون الماشية إلى المكان المقدس للحج. يعود تاريخ هذا اللقب إلى فترة ما قبل الإسلام، حيث كان يُستخدم لتسمية الأشخاص الذين كانوا يزورون الكعبة المشرفة في مكة المكرمة. في الإسلام، يُعتبر الحاجي شخصًا ذا احترام كبير، لأنه يؤدي فريضة الحج، التي تعتبر واحدة من أربع فريصات الإسلامية الكبرى.

in_urdu.name: حاجی
in_urdu.meaning: مزارعین، جوں نے حج کے مقام پر جانوروں کو لے جایا
in_urdu.long_meaning: حاجی ایک لقب ہے جو ان لوگوں کو دیا جاتا ہے جو حج کے مقام پر جانوروں کو لے جاتے ہیں۔ اس لقب کا تعلق ماقبل اسلام کے زمانے سے ہے جب یہ لقب حج کے مقام پر جانوروں کو لے جانے والوں کے لیے استعمال ہوتا تھا۔ اسلام میں حاجی ایک باعترف شخصیت ہے کیونکہ وہ حج کی فرائض کو انجام دیتا ہے جو اسلام کی چھوٹی سے چار فریضوں میں سے ایک ہے۔

in_hindi.name: हाजी
in_hindi.meaning: जो लोग गाय-भैसों को हाजी के स्थान पर ले जाते हैं
in_hindi.long_meaning: हाजी एक प्रकार का नाम है जो उन लोगों को दिया जाता है जो गाय-भैसों को हाजी के स्थान पर ले जाते हैं। इसका इतिहास मुसलमानों के पहले समय से जुड़ा हुआ है जब यह नाम वे लोगों को दिया जाता था जो हाजी के स्थान पर गाय-भैसों को ले जाते थे। इस्लाम में हाजी एक सम्मानित व्यक्ति होता है क्योंकि वह हाजी की फ़रीज़ को पूरा करता है जो इस्लाम की चारों फ़रीज़ों में से एक है।

in_english.name: Haaji
in_english.meaning: Pilgrims who transport animals to the Hajj location, given as a title of honor.
in_english.long_meaning: Haaji is a title of honor given to pilgrims who transport animals to the Hajj location. The etymology of the term Haaji dates back to pre-Islamic times, when it was used to refer to individuals who would visit the Kaaba in Mecca. In Islam, Haaji is considered a title of great respect, as it denotes an individual who has fulfilled the obligation of Hajj, one of the five pillars of Islam.

data.cultural_impact: The title "Haaji" signifies a person who has successfully completed one of the most significant religious duties in Islam. It is a mark of pride not just for the individual, but for their entire community. It speaks volumes about their commitment to their faith and their ability to undertake a long and arduous journey to Mecca. This title is often followed by respect and admiration within the Muslim community.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Haaji" holds immense spiritual significance as it represents a person who has answered the call of God to perform the Hajj pilgrimage. It symbolizes one's obedience to the divine will and their devotion towards God. The experience of performing Hajj is believed to bring Muslims closer to their creator and to wipe away their sins. The journey itself is full of spiritual rituals, from the symbolic stoning of Satan to the circling of the Kaaba, all of which reinforce the connection between the pilgrim and their Creator.
